steps: Active bleed: resuscitate (IV access, fluids/blood, transfuse to Hb ~70 g/L threshold); correct coagulopathy.
Urgent endoscopy (within 24 h) for haemostasis; IV PPI infusion for high-risk stigmata.
Test and treat H. pylori; stop NSAIDs; continue PPI.
Repeat endoscopy/IR embolisation or surgery for rebleeding.
Risk score (Glasgow-Blatchford/Rockall) guides admission and timing.

drugRefs.dose: 80 mg IV bolus, then 8 mg/hour infusion for 72 h
drugRefs.why: Raises intragastric pH to stabilise clot and reduce rebleeding after endoscopic haemostasis of high-risk stigmata.
Continued acid suppression heals the ulcer; step down from IV once oral intake resumes and re-bleeding risk falls.

drugRefs.dose: transfuse to a restrictive target (Hb ~70 g/L)
drugRefs.why: Restrictive transfusion improves outcomes in acute upper-GI bleeding except in significant cardiovascular disease.

drugRefs.dose: 20 mg PO twice daily for 7 days
drugRefs.why: Acid suppression enhances antibiotic efficacy in H. pylori eradication.

drugRefs.dose: 1 g PO twice daily for 7 days
drugRefs.why: Component of first-line PPI-based triple therapy for confirmed H. pylori.

drugRefs.dose: 500 mg PO twice daily for 7 days
drugRefs.why: Component of first-line PPI-based triple therapy (use metronidazole if penicillin-allergic or high clarithromycin resistance).
